paragraphs.text: Where the people then encamped, {Num 33:49} and where the Midianites sometime, by the counsel of Balaam, Satan’s spell man, outwitted the Israelites by setting fair women before them, who soon drew them into those two sister sins, idolatry and adultery. {Num 25:1-2; Num 25:18}
paragraphs.anchor: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim.

paragraphs.text: Not twelve, as Num 13:2-3, for those were too many by ten; and did much harm among the people.
paragraphs.anchor: Two men.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Silently. Silence is oft no small virtue; and he is a rare man who can both keep and give counsel.
paragraphs.anchor: To spy secretly.

paragraphs.text: Of which though God had promised to possess them, yet Joshua knew that means was to be used. So 2Sa 5:24. David had a promise of victory over the Philistines; but yet so as that he must fetch a compass behind them; and when he heard "the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberries," then he was to bestir himself.
paragraphs.anchor: Go view the land.

paragraphs.text: Into a harlot’s house.] Or, Hostess, as some render it; but such as stuck not familiarly to entertain strangers. {Heb 11:31 Jas 2:25} Upon her conversion she was advanced to become grandmother to Jesus Christ; who by his purity washeth off all our spots; like as the sun washeth and wipeth away all the ill vapours of the earth and air.
Kings have long ears; their ωτακουσται, informers and intelligencers, are in all places, but especially when Hannibal est ad portas, the enemy is at hand, as now he was.
paragraphs.anchor: And it was told the king of Jericho.

paragraphs.text: As we have cause to conceive. Optimus in dubiis agur timor.
paragraphs.anchor: To search out the country.

paragraphs.text: "To see the nakedness of the land," as Gen 42:9. {See Trapp on "Jos 2:2"}
paragraphs.anchor: For they be come to search out all the country.

paragraphs.text: This was an act of her praiseworthy faith. See Heb 11:31, where it is honourably mentioned, but nothing is said of the lie she told. God layeth the finger of mercy on the scars of our sins; as that painter in the story.
paragraphs.anchor: And the woman took the two men, and hid them.

paragraphs.text: This was no better than an officious lie: yea, four lies she here uttereth together in a breath, - as Jacob also did three, {Gen 27:19-24} - neither can she be excused. That was a worthy speech of a good woman on the rack, as Jerome relateth it, Non ideo negare volo ne peream: sed ideo mentiri nolo, ne peccem. But Rahab was yet but a new convert.
paragraphs.anchor: But I wist not whence they were.

paragraphs.text: See Jos 2:4.
paragraphs.anchor: And it came to pass.

paragraphs.text: {a} Which was built flat in those parts, as they are also at this day in Italy.
paragraphs.anchor: But she had brought them up to the roof of the house.

paragraphs.text: That it might be fully dried, as {Nah 1:10} the wicked are, that they may burn the better: like grapes, they ripen in the sunshine, for the winepress of God’s wrath. {Rev 14:19}
paragraphs.anchor: Which she had laid in order upon the roof.

paragraphs.text: {a} Septuag., δωμα: ut et 1Sa 9:25.

Not once searching the house. Thus God "maketh the wisdom of the wise to perish." {Isa 29:14} See Mat 2:8. Herod went not himself, or sent some assassin to despatch the child Jesus; but sent the wise men to Bethlehem with charge to search, and bring him word. The Dutch have a proverb, Where God intendeth to blind any man, he first closeth up his eyes.
paragraphs.anchor: And the men pursued.

paragraphs.text: so., To take their rest, which in this fright they had little list to. "Sleep on now, take your rest," saith our Saviour by an irony to his drowsy disciples; q.d., Do so, if you can at least, now, with so many swords and halberds about your ears. {Mar 14:41}
paragraphs.anchor: And before they were laid down

paragraphs.text: She had a full assurance both of knowledge, {as Luk 1:1} and of faith, {as Heb 6:10; Heb 11:31} when many Israelites staggered and distrusted the promise. "God hath mercy on whom he will have mercy," &c. {Rom 9:15; Rom 9:18}
paragraphs.anchor: I know that the Lord hath given you the land.

paragraphs.text: Historiae fidae monitrices. Succurrat illud … Mutato nomine de te fabula narratur.
paragraphs.anchor: For we have heard.

paragraphs.text: As for our idols, they are very vanities, and cannot deliver us. The Tyrians, afraid their Apollo should forsake them at that time when Alexander besieged their city, chained and nailed that idol to a post, that they might be sure of it; but all would not do.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord your God, he is God.

paragraphs.text: Sυσσημον, as Mar 14:44. Signum consignans, de composito datum. As for the familiar conference that here passed betwixt these spies and Rahab, we need not question how they could so easily understand one another, being of two several nations. For, first, the language of the Canaanites, Phoenicians, Philistines, differed not much from the Hebrew, which Jerome {a} rightly calleth Omnium linguarum matricem, the mother tongue. See Plautus in "Paenulo," act v. And then, it is not unlikely that these spies had learned the language of Canaan, by conversing with those conquered Amorites on this side Jordan.
paragraphs.anchor: And give me a true token.

paragraphs.text: {a} In cap. iii. Sophoniae.

Man is ζωον φιλοζωον, a creature that would fain live, said Aesop. Quis vitam non vult? said Augustine. The Gibeonites were desirous to live upon any terms. {Jos 9:3-14} Rahab’s greatest care was for her kindred, because unconverted. Augustine professeth that he would not for the gain of a million of worlds be an atheist for half an hour: because he knew not but God might in that time call him to account.
paragraphs.anchor: And that ye will save alive.

paragraphs.text: On this condition we assure thee of safety. God’s promises also are with a condition, which is as an oar in a boat, or stern of a ship, and turneth the promise another way.
paragraphs.anchor: If ye utter not this our business.

paragraphs.text: In an obscure nook, among the poorer sort of people: for this harlot Rahab had not got such an estate as Phryne had, who offered at her own charge to repair the ruined walls of Thebes, if these words only might have been inscribed on them, "Alexander overturned these walls, and Phryne set them up again." {a}
paragraphs.anchor: For her house was upon the town wall.

paragraphs.text: Where Providence had placed her for such a purpose as this: for it is God that appointeth the bounds of men’s habitations. {Act 17:26}
paragraphs.anchor: And she dwelt upon the wall.

paragraphs.text: {a} O μεν Aλεξανδρος κατεσκαψε, η δε φρυνη ανωκοδο μησεν.
This, say some, was spoken after the men were down, in the still of the night, without the wall. {Jos 2:18} But what a fool was he who said, Mισω σοφην γυναικα, I hate a discreet woman!
paragraphs.anchor: Get you to the mountain.

paragraphs.text: q.d, Great haste though we have, yet will we clear up the terms whereunto we have sworn, to prevent the danger or rebut the suspicion of perjury. An oath is not to be taken but with a great deal of caution and circumspection, {Gen 24:3-5} not in jest, but in judgment, {Jer 4:2 Isa 48:1} not rashly and unadvisedly, {Lev 5:4 1Sa 14:39; 1Sa 14:44} as those that swear in heat and choler, when they should with fear, {Deu 10:20} discerning the nature of an oath, the necessity, the conditions and circumstances.
paragraphs.anchor: We will be blameless of this thine oath

paragraphs.text: Who, if not there found when we storm the town, shall perish at their own peril. So shall all not found to be of the family of faith, and within God’s doors. The devil sweeps all that are out of the covenant.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt bring thy father, &c.
